brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books (load rating)
requirements.evidence: The build is two full hex bases with two notch drawers. The configurator checks fit and collisions only, not load, so no 50 kg rating can be verified or claimed. The build is not a shelf unit with open shelving for books; it is a small drawer block.

Two notch drawers (hex-drawer-body-notch x2, from notch frames hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm at cell (0,1) and hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf at cell (1,-1)) on two full hex bases at (0,0) and (1,0). check_build meshClash clear, no errors.

finish.summary: I built a two-base block with two notch drawers, which meets the two-drawer requirement and passes the mesh check. I could not verify the 50 kg book rating, since the configurator does not check load, and the build has no open shelving for books, so that requirement is unmet. Drawers in this system sit on the cut face of a half base only when that face is exposed; the working route was two touching full bases with notch drawer frames between them.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
